note: Holdings-relevant market news, researched daily by the intel agent (multi-theme sweep: precious metals, HK tech, SGX/Singapore, rare earths, macro) with sources. The "actionable" line relates each item to this specific portfolio. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Silver holds ~$61/oz after a ~6% weekly rebound; Silver Institute pegs a widening 46.3Moz 2026 deficit, JPMorgan sees ~$81 average
items.summary: Silver traded around $61.36/oz on 7 July, off a ~$67.75 level a month ago but still up sharply year-on-year, after logging its best week in over five weeks on the soft June jobs print. The structural bull thesis is intact: the Silver Institute projects a 46.3Moz market deficit in 2026 (vs 40.3Moz in 2025) and J.P. Morgan models silver averaging ~$81/oz this year. Volatility remains extreme after June's crash halved the metal from January's ~$120 peak.
items.actionable: This is the core levered-silver thesis working again — the ~6% bounce plus a widening physical deficit supports holding, but June proved the downside, so keep leverage sized so a retest of ~$58 cannot force liquidation ahead of the 14 July CPI.

items.headline: June FOMC minutes land today (US); July hold priced ~73%, a hike by December still ~two-thirds
items.summary: The minutes of the Fed's June meeting — Chair Kevin Warsh's first, where rates were held at 3.50%-3.75% with a hawkish dot plot (9 of 19 officials see a 2026 hike, median end-2026 rate ~3.8%) — are released 8 July at 2:00pm ET and are the only on-record read on a possible September move. CME FedWatch shows ~73% odds of a hold at the 28-29 July meeting and ~27% for a 25bp hike, with roughly two-thirds odds of at least one hike by December. June CPI on 14 July is the next binary catalyst.
items.actionable: Mark 8 July (minutes) and 14 July (June CPI) as the two hawkish-risk dates for the levered silver stack — a hot CPI would revive the hike repricing that crushed metals in June, so keep option/stop protection on through the print.

items.headline: Gold steadies near $4,150; Goldman trims year-end target to ~$4,900 as Fed cuts fade, but PBoC keeps buying
items.summary: Gold is consolidating around $4,000-4,175 after June's ~11% slide. Goldman cut its year-end target to ~$4,900 (from higher) after concluding the Fed is unlikely to cut in 2026 and citing fading gold-ETF inflows, while J.P. Morgan stays far more bullish (~$6,000 by Q4). The People's Bank of China reportedly ramped official gold buying to ~8 tonnes in April (from ~1t/month), a supportive central-bank bid under the price.
items.actionable: Gold's central-bank demand floor cushions the GDX/miner sleeve, but a hawkish Fed caps upside — treat $4,000 as the line that matters for the miners and don't expect gold to rescue silver on its own.

items.headline: June payrolls miss at +57,000 (consensus ~115,000) with -74,000 in revisions; near-term Fed hike odds crumble
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls rose just 57,000 in June — roughly half consensus — while April/May were revised down a combined 74,000. Unemployment ticked down to 4.2%, but only because labor-force participation fell to 61.5%, the lowest since March 2021. Traders scaled back tightening bets sharply, effectively taking a July hike largely off the table (~27%) and pushing September into doubt.
items.actionable: The soft labor print is the single most metal-friendly data point of the window — it directly reduces the hike-repricing risk that crushed your silver stack in June, arguing for holding rather than de-risking into the bounce.

items.headline: Tencent's near-daily buyback continues into July — 465,000 shares for HK$204.8m on 6 July after ~HK$500m tranches through end-June
items.summary: An HKEX filing shows Tencent repurchased about 465,000 shares for HK$204.8m on Monday 6 July (a lighter day), following ~1.1-1.2m-share, ~HK$500m daily tranches on 2, 3 and 30 June. The relentless cadence runs under the ~912m-share (10%) mandate approved at the 13 May 2026 AGM, mechanically shrinking the count as the stock trades around HK$450-460.
items.actionable: Hold 0700.HK; the persistent buyback bid offers downside support around HK$450-460 — consider adding on dips into that zone rather than chasing rallies.

items.headline: China formalizes rare-earth export enforcement (MOFCOM reporting mechanism live 1 July); MP & USA Rare Earth remain on the control list
items.summary: Effective 1 July 2026, China's MOFCOM launched a mechanism rewarding tips on export-control violations — unlicensed exports, transshipment and disguised shipments of strategic minerals — tightening the regime after June's blacklisting of 10 US firms including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. New licensing now covers samarium, gadolinium and lutetium compounds; two Japanese nationals were detained in May over alleged smuggling.
items.actionable: Tighter Chinese enforcement raises the scarcity premium on ex-China supply and validates the Western onshoring thesis — treat pullbacks in MP/LYC.AX/UUUU on the watchlist as scale-in candidates, while 6680.HK (JL MAG) faces the export-cap headwind.

items.headline: Straits Times Index hits record ~5,244 as banks lead; SGX unveils retail-access reforms
items.summary: The STI rose ~1% on the week to a fresh all-time high near 5,244 on Friday 3 July, led by DBS and OCBC on resilient net interest margins, with SGX, OCBC and ST Engineering the week's focus names. SGX announced structural changes aimed at improving retail-investor access. The global backdrop was supportive with the S&P 500 near 7,500.
items.actionable: A broad tailwind for the SGX sleeve (DBS, Singtel, REITs, developers) — but with DBS at record levels and ~2.2x book into 6 August results, favor adding to S-REITs (which benefit from falling SORA) over paying up for the banks here.

items.headline: Oil slides toward 4-month lows (Brent ~$72-73, WTI ~$70.5) on OPEC+ hikes and restored Gulf supply, though WTI bounced +2.9% on 7 July
items.summary: Brent traded around $72-73 and WTI ~$70.5 (a +2.9% bounce on 7 July) — near 4-month lows and down sharply from the ~$96-126 wartime peaks as the Israel/Iran risk premium unwound. OPEC+ approved another +188kbpd for next month and Saudi Aramco cut its Asian Arab Light OSP by $11/bbl as Gulf exports neared pre-war levels. Falling oil is disinflationary but also drains the geopolitical safe-haven bid for metals.
items.actionable: Don't count on an Iran-risk premium to rescue silver — the bull case now rests on cooling US data and fading hike odds; watch Hormuz/OPEC+ headlines mainly as a two-way volatility source and a disinflation tailwind for the CPI print.

items.headline: Energy Fuels lands $725M US Office of Strategic Capital financing; begins heavy-REE circuit build at White Mesa in July
items.summary: Energy Fuels received a conditional $725M financing commitment from the US Office of Strategic Capital, tied to a planned acquisition of Australian Strategic Materials and its Korean metal/alloy/magnet facilities. From July 2026 it is modifying White Mesa Phase 1 circuits to add heavy rare earths (Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy) alongside NdPr, while uranium output reached ~1.6Mlb by 30 June, within its 1.5-2.5Mlb guidance.
items.actionable: Washington keeps putting a financing floor under Western rare-earth economics — a starter UUUU or MP position funded from the cash pile is reasonable, but note UUUU's dilution/integration overhang from the ASM deal is worth letting settle first.

items.headline: SMIC guides Q2 revenue +14-16% on AI-chip demand; shares ~HK$76 with a Buy consensus
items.summary: SMIC — China's largest and the world's third-largest foundry — guided Q2 revenue up ~14-16% QoQ on strong AI-driven demand and price increases, prioritizing capacity expansion (~50k wafers/month/year) over dividends. Shares traded ~HK$75.75 on 6 July within a 52-week range of HK$43.70-93.50, carrying a consensus Buy rating (16 buy / 4 sell).
items.actionable: Maintain 0981.HK as a preferred southbound AI/semiconductor-localization vehicle, but size for volatility (the stock swings HK$70-80 intraday vs a HK$93.50 high); a Fed-cut repricing is the main index-level upside trigger.

items.headline: Xiaomi tops 30,000 EV deliveries in June for a third straight month; YU7 line ramping toward 550k FY26 target
items.summary: Xiaomi EV delivered over 30,000 units in June 2026, its third consecutive 30k+ month, keeping the 550,000-unit full-year target in play (Jan-May: ~150,317, +13.5% YoY). The YU7 SUV range expanded with a cheaper standard edition (from RMB233,500, a Model Y rival) and a high-end YU7 GT, with in-stock cars now delivering within hours.
items.actionable: Hold 1810.HK; monthly delivery prints and the YU7 ramp are the key catalysts — wait for evidence of a H2 volume acceleration before adding, as the FY target still needs a strong second half.

items.headline: Yangzijiang books $1.03bn new orders YTD ($22.3bn orderbook); Seatrium sits on a S$15.5bn orderbook and >S$32bn pipeline
items.summary: Yangzijiang has booked 17 vessels worth $1.03bn year-to-date against a $4.5bn 2026 win target, with an outstanding orderbook of $22.3bn, 69% clean-energy vessels. Seatrium reported a S$15.5bn orderbook at 31 March with a pipeline above S$32bn and guidance of S$10-11bn annual wins through 2026-28 on the offshore-energy upcycle.
items.actionable: Both core marine holdings are riding a multi-year orderbook cushion — a reason to hold through oil-price noise, since backlog (not spot crude) drives near-term earnings visibility.

items.headline: Bitcoin starts H2 near a 21-month low (~$60-64k) after the hawkish Fed removed 2026 rate-cut hopes; crypto sentiment lifts off Extreme Fear
items.summary: Bitcoin began the second half near $60,000 after a fresh 21-month low, trading ~$61.7-64k on 6-7 July, with the sell-off tied to Warsh's June hold removing 2026 rate-cut expectations. Stress signals include a 43-month-low realized P&L ratio, though the crypto Fear & Greed index has recovered to 27 (Fear) from ~12 (Extreme Fear).
items.actionable: Bitcoin's slump is a useful risk-off/rate-sensitivity gauge for the book — its stabilization off Extreme Fear is a mild tell that the same hawkish-Fed pressure weighing on metals may be easing; keep any crypto sizing small.

items.headline: Lynas Q3 FY26 NdPr +32% and revenue +115%; CEO Lacaze steps down with Le Roux interim as ex-China supply re-rates
items.summary: Lynas reported Q3 FY26 (to 31 March) NdPr output up 32% YoY to 1,996t and revenue up 115% YoY to A$265M, its strongest since FY22, and said it expects higher rare-earth prices after US backing of MP Materials. Long-serving CEO Amanda Lacaze stepped down on 1 July, with operations chief Pol Le Roux taking over on an interim basis to execute the downstream 'Towards 2030' magnet expansion.
items.actionable: Lynas remains the cleanest ex-China separated-REE producer with strong fundamentals, but the CEO transition adds execution uncertainty — a watchlist hold rather than a chase, with the VanEck REMX pullback (~21% off its high) offering a lower-risk basket entry.
